mission: Comm station. Ben cycles frequencies and catches fragmentary Jedi outpost reports — anomalous Force behaviour at multiple nexuses, the Valley of the Jedi destabilising. Desh plots the disturbances radiating outward from the Corridor. Luke's coded message arrives: 'Sensing disturbances at multiple nexuses. Report status.' Ben stares at the reply field without typing.
why_now: The crisis has to go galactic on the page for Torin's Scene 2 argument to have the stakes it needs. The Order now knows something is wrong, and Ben now has to decide what to say about it.
conflict: The reports match the pattern the group has been mapping. The Valley of the Jedi — the place where the Reformations began — is responding to the seal's failure. Ben has the vocabulary for what he is seeing; Luke has a question he has earned the right to ask.
turning_point: Luke's coded message arrives on Ben's personal frequency. Ben stares at the reply field without typing. H13 resolves — Veraine heading for Veranthos is no longer a private problem.
opening_hook: Ben cycles through comm channels and catches fragmentary reports he can only half-decrypt — Jedi outposts at multiple nexuses reporting anomalous Force behavior. The wrongness isn't just here anymore.
closing_hook: Luke's personal message, brief and coded: 'Sensing disturbances at multiple nexuses. Report status.' Ben stares at the message for a long time. He doesn't answer.
emotional_trajectory: Strategic alarm -> scope expanding -> the weight of withholding from Luke deepening

stakes.personal: Ben's withholding becoming harder to maintain as the crisis affects the broader Order
stakes.interpersonal: The group recognising that their local mission has galaxy-wide consequences
stakes.external: The seal's failure is reaching Force nexuses across the galaxy

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — comm station, hyperspace transit
sensory_details: Static-filled comm intercepts from multiple sectors; Luke's message coded but readable, brief and controlled; Ben's datapad holding an empty reply draft; the wrongness a permanent background pressure now, no longer surprising — weather rather than event
action_beats: Ben cycles through comm frequencies and catches fragmentary distress reports from Jedi outposts across the galaxy
Desh pulls up a galactic map and plots each reported disturbance — the pattern radiating outward from the Corridor
Luke's coded message arrives on Ben's personal frequency and Ben stares at the reply field without typing
notes: SP4 intensifying — Ben's withholding moves from editorial discretion toward disobedience as the crisis expands. The parallel to Gavran's secrecy should be felt without being named by Ben. Anti-pattern: do not stage Luke on comm as a speaking voice; his presence is a coded line and an empty reply field. Rotate Force-wrongness metaphor family: weather/pressure (a migraine that does not break, pressure at altitude, a front pushing through) rather than acoustic or navigational registers. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, construct an explanation to himself for why he is not replying. The not-replying is the scene; the justification is Ch15 sc3's work.
